headline: Wet, windy Friday, a stronger storm Saturday night, and cooler weather next week.
summary: A very mild air mass is parked over the region, with a cold front stalled offshore. Behind it, a series of storms from the Pacific is heading toward western Washington. The first arrives Friday with rain and breezy to windy conditions. A stronger system follows late Saturday into Saturday night, bringing the most widespread wind of the period. The Olympics are likely to get the heaviest rain, and coastal areas and gaps in the terrain will see the strongest gusts. The Skokomish River is expected to rise back above flood stage Friday into the weekend, and showers linger into Monday before tapering off. Temperatures are expected to drift back toward normal next week. Forecasters are fairly confident through Saturday, but confidence drops after Tuesday as the computer models begin to disagree.
